metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: not_specified (procedure given for bug-finding/fixing use case, but no numeric volume or scope cap on contributions generally)

evidence.quote: AI agents MUST NOT add Signed-off-by tags. Only humans can legally certify the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO).

The human submitter is responsible for:

* Reviewing all AI-generated code
* Ensuring compliance with licensing requirements
* Adding their own Signed-off-by tag to certify the DCO
* Taking full responsibility for the contribution

domains.reasoning: The document explicitly names AI-assisted code contributions, requires human review, human sign-off, and full human accountability for the submitted work, satisfying both supervision level and accountability holder.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for meeting/notetaker bots
domains.reasoning: The document is scoped to AI coding assistants for kernel development and never mentions meeting recording, notetaker bots, or closed/small-group discussion capture.

evidence.quote:

domains.reasoning: This file only cross-references a separate document (generated-content.rst, not in scope for this assessment) for AI-generated content guidance; it sets no rule of its own about documentation, blogs, or design assets.

unscoped_statements.quote: AI tools helping with Linux kernel development should follow the standard kernel development process

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy is fairly specific about AI-assisted code contributions and autonomous bug-finding/fixing (mandating human review, human sign-off/DCO, an Assisted-by attribution tag, and forbidding the AI from autonomously submitting anything), but it is silent on notetaker bots, general content generation, moderation, broader review practices, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data use.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
